A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBS measurement and batch-size warmup study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; v3 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original OLMo CBS and gradient-noise measurements, warmup/control training experiments, and downstream evaluations in Figures 1–6, Tables 1–2, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the training comparisons, downstream evaluations, and appendix checkpoint plots.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the stated CBS-selection rule: a candidate may now incur up to epsilon additional loss, whereas v1's inequality required an epsilon improvement. This changes the written acceptance condition; branching, square-root learning-rate scaling, and batch-size doubling remain unchanged. A change to the experimental implementation is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same pretraining and mid-training tasks, C4 and Pile evaluations, and all 13 downstream BPB tasks listed in Appendix E. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain McCandlish et al.'s gradient-noise estimator and the same fixed small-batch and large-batch controls. The newly cited Li et al. work is discussed theoretically, not evaluated as an additional baseline.

E3.justification: The corrected loss-tolerance inequality in Section 3.1 revises the reported procedure for extracting CBS from experimental losses. Run budgets, checkpoints, tolerance magnitude, downstream metrics and splits, and the 168B/503B-token warmup thresholds remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun using a different criterion.

E4.justification: The checkpoint-wise loss curves, model-size comparisons, and estimator-distribution histograms are retained. v3 discusses sensitivity studies and methodological extensions as future work; it adds no completed ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same CBS bracketing intervals and 95% noise-scale confidence intervals, with the same 4096-batch averaging and distributional assumptions in Appendix B. The new checklist restates existing reporting rather than adding runs, seeds, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all main-text and appendix plots retain their results. For example, warmup pretraining/mid-training losses remain 2.5891/2.5433 with 43% fewer gradient steps. The threshold-provenance footnote supplies no revised numerical result.

T1.justification: The formal CBS definition changes from L_k >= L_{k*} + epsilon to L_{k*} <= L_k + epsilon, a mathematically non-equivalent correction. The stated assumptions and all three propositions and proofs in Appendix D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: direct local CBS measurement, similar CBS evolution across model sizes, unreliable gradient-noise estimates, and warmup achieving comparable or better loss with 43% fewer steps. The expanded conclusion adds future directions without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: A new footnote qualifies the connection between reported CBS measurements and warmup thresholds: thresholds came from preliminary measurements, and insensitivity to their precise values is assumed rather than tested. The conclusion expands discussion of measurement sensitivity/bias and conditions under which noise scale might remain useful.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the preliminary origin of warmup thresholds and that expensive training runs were not restarted after measurements changed. It clarifies GPU-divisible batch sizes and adds a conditional code-release plan in the checklist; it does not establish that code has been released. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Li et al. (2024), 'Surge phenomenon in optimal learning rate and batch size scaling,' to support square-root Adam scaling. It also corrects the cost comparison from 'more' to 'less' expensive than full-run sweeps and refines the critique of prior noise-scale methodology.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording corrections, revises the scaling and GPU-divisibility explanations, expands the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and a checklist. The research narrative and organization of Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–E remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The scientific figures and table structures are preserved. Changes include minor caption/reference wording, spacing and text reflow around expanded passages and footnotes, an updated conference footer, and appended checklist pages.

improvement.justification: Correcting the CBS acceptance inequality and the contradictory Adam scaling description improves technical consistency. The threshold-provenance disclosure and expanded limitations improve transparency, although threshold sensitivity remains untested. These are useful, bounded gains; the empirical evidence and principal conclusions are unchanged.
